newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Arafat gave green light to bomb.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Arafat gave green light to bomb.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority of indirectly giving a green light to groups behind a blast on Friday in central Tel Aviv in which four people were killed.

"I said these organisations understood from the things that were said to them they had the approval of the Palestinian Authority...There is no doubt they acted on the basis of that understanding," he told reporters.
Netanyahu did not say he would halt peace talks with the Palestinians.

"The peace process is threatened not by the periodic misunderstandings, disagreements or impasses. It is threatened by the mentality that says if we have a disagreement with someone we can go and blow them up," he said.

"It is threatened by the idea that violence is sanctioned as part of negotiations. It is threatened by the idea that you can go and kill women and children in a downtown cafe -- that is what threatens the peace process," he added.
Police said a caller to their Tel Aviv office had claimed responsibility for the attack in the name of the Islamic militant group Hamas.
Israeli security forces had been on high alert nationwide to prevent unrest by Palestinians opposed to Netanyahu's breaking ground this week on a Jewish settlement on the outskirts of Jerusalem.

But visiting the wounded at a Tel Aviv hospital, Netanyahu said he believed attacks would not stop even were he to halt the construction for Jews on the Jerusalem hilltop which Israel calls Har Homa and the Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

"The army's security branches warned that terrorist organisations understood that they got a green light from the Palestinian Authority and to my sorrow it's become clear that they were right and the terrorist organisations on the strength of that green light acted," Netanyahu said.
"I want to say also that the Palestinian Authority did not do a thing or half a thing to refute that understanding and therefore it bears very heavy responsibility."
